result.summary: The street is a narrow residential corridor with a sidewalk on one side and a park on the other. Pedestrian safety is compromised by utility poles obstructing the narrow walkway and a lack of marked crossings at the visible intersection.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Utility poles are placed directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to step into the street or navigate around them.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks marked crosswalks, increasing risk for pedestrians crossing between the residential block and the park.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the park edge may obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching motorists.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Obstruction Removal
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk on the residential side and relocate utility poles to ensure a clear, accessible path of travel.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a paved sidewalk separated from the roadway by a vegetated buffer with mature trees, providing good physical separation. However, the walkway is partially obstructed by organic debris and an encroaching parked vehicle, and there is a lack of visible crossing infrastructure or street lighting.

hazards.name: Parked vehicle encroachment
hazards.description: A vehicle is parked extremely close to the sidewalk edge, potentially narrowing the accessible path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Organic debris on walkway
hazards.description: Accumulated leaves and twigs on the sidewalk surface can create slip hazards and obscure pavement defects.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Maintenance
interventions.description: Regular removal of leaves and debris to ensure a clear and safe walking surface.

interventions.title: Parking Enforcement
interventions.description: Ensure vehicles are parked correctly within designated areas to prevent encroachment on the pedestrian walkway.

result.summary: The street is a narrow residential corridor with row houses on one side and a park-like green space on the other. While a sidewalk exists on the residential side, it is narrow and lacks a buffer from parked cars, and the opposite side lacks a paved walkway entirely.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A chair is placed on the narrow sidewalk on the right, reducing the effective walking width.

hazards.name: Missing Walkway
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a paved sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to walk on uneven dirt or in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street under the trees

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars and large tree trunks create sightline issues for pedestrians attempting to cross the street.

interventions.title: New Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a continuous and safe walking path adjacent to the park.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential and park-adjacent environment.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crosswalk with curb extensions to improve visibility and provide a safe crossing point to the park.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a wide concrete walkway adjacent to residential buildings, characterized by significant pavement degradation and cracking. While the path is wide, the lack of maintenance and presence of litter detract from the overall safety and comfort for walkers.

hazards.name: Uneven Pavement
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface is heavily cracked and uneven, creating significant trip hazards.

hazards.name: Litter and Debris
hazards.description: Trash bags and loose debris are present on the walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Near the fire hydrant and in the alleyway

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and level the cracked concrete to provide a smooth, accessible walking surface.

interventions.title: Waste Management
interventions.description: Provide public trash receptacles and regular cleaning services to keep the walkway clear of debris.
